    Desk · sending the reports

    The Mailing List

    The tab where the owner sends the reports to the people who signed up on bablytics.com: Sync pulls the list down from Firestore, the app drafts the day's message with the right PDF attached, a dry run shows exactly what would go out, and a confirmed click sends it — by hand, in batches of fifty blind copies, with the research-tool footer and an unsubscribe line on every email. Nothing is ever sent automatically.

    Since round 26 the reports the app writes can leave the machine one way on purpose: by email, to people who asked for them. The list has two halves that never touch each other except through the owner's clicks. On the website, Get the reports by email writes one record per address into a small Firebase database that only the owner can read. In the app, the Mailing list tab is where that list is pulled down, kept, and written to: Sync fetches the sign-ups and the unsubscribe requests, the Send panel drafts today's message — subject, a few lines from the day's JSON, the day's PDF — a Dry run renders the exact text and counts the recipients without opening a connection, and Send, after a confirm dialog, hands the message to your own SMTP account in batches of fifty blind-copied addresses. That is the whole mechanism. There is no schedule, no queue and no service behind it: if nobody clicks, nothing goes out.

    Where it lives#

    The tab is Mail in the main navigation (the page is titled Mailing list), beside the other desks. It has three panels, stacked top to bottom: the Send panel (Send the report, with the kind selector Morning Briefing · Evening Court · Weekend report · Custom note, a date, Reload draft, today's draft, the attachment list, the recipient count, an optional Test to address and the Dry run and Send… buttons); the subscriber table (Subscribers, with the counts strip, search, status filter and the + Add · Import CSV · Export CSV · Sync from Firestore controls); and the Send log, one row per send. The connection details — SMTP host, port, user, From address, TLS, and the Firebase project id, web API key and owner email — are on the Settings page, and the two passwords are never in the app at all: they are read from .env at the moment they are needed. What leaves the machine, and to whom, is spelled out on Data & privacy.

    How a name gets on the list#

    Three ways in, one table. The website form writes a document to the Firestore collection subscribers — id = the first 32 hex characters of SHA-256 of the lowercased address, so an address can only be there once; fields email, emailLower, firstName, style, reports: {morning, evening, weekend}, consent: true, source: "bablytics.com", createdAt (nothing else — no user-agent, no IP) — and the app's Sync copies it into the local subscribers table with source = web. You can also Add a person by hand (source = manual, consent stamped at the moment you add them, because you are vouching for it) or Import a CSV (source = import). Whatever the source, the row has the same shape:

    ColumnValuesNotes
    emailunique, case-insensitiveStored lower-cased; Sean@Example.com and sean@example.com are one row.
    first_nameoptionalSo a future template can say hello; the v1 body does not use it.
    styleintraday · swing · long_term · mix · emptyThe form's "How do you trade" — the same four values as the mandate; Day, Long-term and friends normalise to the keys. Informational in v1; no send is filtered by it.
    reports{morning, evening, weekend} flags, all on by defaultWhich kinds the person asked for. A morning send goes only to rows with morning on, and so on; a custom note goes to every active row.
    statusactive · unsubscribed · bouncedOnly active rows ever receive anything. bounced is a label you set by hand after a provider rejection; nothing sets it automatically.
    sourceweb · manual · importWhere the row came from.
    firestore_id · consent_at · created_at · updated_at · unsubscribed_at · notesbookkeepingThe web document's id and its createdAt (kept as the consent time); when the row was unsubscribed; free notes — the sync writes "unsubscribed via bablytics.com (date)" there, and flags a web document that somehow lacks consent: true.

    The subscriber table#

    The table lists every row with its status and source, a search box that matches the address, the first name and the notes, and a status filter (active · unsubscribed · bounced); the header shows the counts per status and how many active rows want each report kind. Per row: a toggle button — Unsubscribe on an active row, Reactivate on an unsubscribed one — that flips active ⇄ unsubscribed in one click, and Remove, which asks first and then deletes the row outright. (Changing a row's name, style, report flags or notes is done by importing a CSV line for that address — the import updates an existing row in place — or through PATCH /api/maillist/{id}; the table itself has no edit form. The API refuses a new address that already belongs to another row.) Removing is the right move for a typo or a test address; for a person who asked to stop, use the toggle — a row that stays in the table as unsubscribed is what keeps the next Sync or Import from quietly putting them back on (below).

    Export and import CSV#

    Export CSV downloads bablytics-subscribers.csv — header email,first_name,style,reports,status, one row per subscriber sorted by address, reports written as morning|evening|weekend; the status filter applies, so you can export the active list alone. Import CSV takes the same file back, and most other people's files too: the header is detected by an email-ish column name (email, e-mail, email address, mail …) and the other columns are matched by alias (name, first, firstname → first name; mandate, trading style, how do you trade → style; which reports → reports; state → status; note → notes); a file with no header is read positionally in the export's order. Rules: an invalid address is skipped and reported with its line number; a duplicate within the file is skipped; a status column is honoured when present in the safe direction only — re-importing your own export restores unsubscribes, but a stale file saying active never re-activates a row that is unsubscribed or bounced (the line is reported; reactivating is the toggle's job) — and otherwise new rows become active while existing rows keep their status; an existing row is only updated in the columns the file actually has. The result reads added · updated · skipped · rows plus the per-line errors.

    Sync from Firestore#

    Sync is a read of the website's database onto your machine, and the only reader it has. When you click it:

    1. Sign in as the owner. The app calls Firebase's identity endpoint (accounts:signInWithPassword) with the owner email from Settings and FIREBASE_OWNER_PASSWORD from .env, and gets back a short-lived ID token. The rules let exactly that account read; a browser, including the sign-up page itself, can only create.
    2. List both collections over Firestore's REST API with that token — subscribers and unsubscribe_requests, paged, every document. No SDK, no service account, no admin key on the machine.
    3. Then, and only then, write locally. Every subscriber document is upserted by address: a new address is added as active · web with its consent time; an address already in the table has its name, style, report flags and Firestore id refreshed but keeps its status — a sync never re-activates someone you or they unsubscribed. Every unsubscribe_requests document then marks its address unsubscribed (with the request date in the notes); a request for an address that is not on the list changes nothing — it is not invented as a row. Both reads finish before the first write, so a failed network call leaves the table exactly as it was.

    The result shows added · updated · unsubscribed, how many documents were fetched from each collection, any error lines (a document without consent: true is imported but flagged in its notes and listed here), and synced_at, which the tab shows as "last synced". Sync is a click; it is not run for you before a send or on any timer, which is why the habit is Sync, then draft. Until the Firebase project exists and its four values are set (project id, web API key, owner email in Settings; the password in .env) the button answers with a plain message saying which of the four is missing — 409 from the API — and the website form, for its part, degrades to a mailto: request that you add by hand.

    The daily send: draft → dry run → confirm#

    The Send panel is built so that the owner's job is to read and approve, never to write from scratch. The flow, in the order the buttons sit:

    1. Pick the kind and the date. The selector offers Morning Briefing, Evening Court, Weekend report and Custom note; the date defaults to today in Eastern time. The panel fetches the draft (GET /api/maillist/draft?kind=&date=) and fills in the fields.
    2. Read the draft. For a morning it is Bablytics Morning Briefing — Fri Aug 21, 2026 as the subject; the body is the headline, the top stock lead and the top option lead with entry and final grade, the first sentence of the Executive's memo, a slate line ("10 stock leads · 10 option leads — every lead carries its entry, stop and target in the attached PDF") and the standing disclaimer — all read from that day's briefing.json. An evening draft reads the close packet and the court report instead: the book at the close against SPY, the best and worst call with the member's name, the first line of tomorrow's watch. A weekend draft finds the Week in Review or the Week-Ahead Prospectus for that Saturday or Sunday (and the other day of the same weekend) and takes its headline, reckoning, best and worst week or the top leads and the Monday watch. Custom is an empty subject and body for a note of your own, still ending in the disclaimer. Every field is editable before you send.
    3. Check the attachment. The draft names the right PDF — data/reports/Bablytics-Morning-Briefing-<date>.pdf, Bablytics-Evening-Court-<date>.pdf, the Week-In-Review or Week-Ahead-Prospectus file, or the same report under runs/<date>/ — and lists it with its size. If it is not there yet the draft says so in plain words ("Morning Briefing PDF not found …"), the body carries a bracketed warning, and the draft's ok flag is false: generate or collect the report first. The allowed roots are data/reports/ and runs/ and nothing else — an attachment from anywhere else is refused before anything is built, and each file is capped at 20 MB, the message at 24 MB.
    4. See who would get it. The recipient count is the number of active rows whose report flag for this kind is on (every active row for a custom note). It comes from the local table and nowhere else.
    5. Dry run. POST /api/maillist/send with dry_run: true — the default — renders the exact message text (body plus the footer below), resolves and measures the attachments, counts the recipients and the batches, reports whether SMTP is configured, and returns all of it for the preview. It never opens a connection. This is the moment to read what people will read.
    6. Send → confirm → result. Send… first re-runs the dry run on the server (so the dialog shows the exact recipient count and the resolved attachments with their sizes) and then raises a confirm dialog naming the kind, the subject, the recipient count and batch count, the From address and the attachments; its button reads Send to N recipients. The button is disabled, with the reason, while SMTP is unconfigured; Dry run always works. Confirming posts the same payload with dry_run: false and confirm: true — the server refuses a real send without both, and refuses it again if SMTP is unconfigured (409) or the recipient list is empty (400). The app then connects to your SMTP host (STARTTLS on port 587 by default, implicit TLS on 465, the password from SMTP_PASSWORD) and sends one message per batch of fifty addresses: From and To are your From address, the recipients are in Bcc, so nobody on the list sees anybody else. The result — ok, partial (a provider refused some addresses; they are listed) or failed — is shown and logged whatever happened.

    A test send is the same call with test_to set to one address — the Test to field beside the buttons; your own address, say — which replaces the list for that send (the dialog then reads Send the test) and is logged with a "[test → you]" suffix. It is the cheap way to see the real thing in a real inbox before the list does.

    Morning Briefing — Fri Aug 21, 2026

Two rulings fired Thursday and nothing closed, so a book that reads +0.55% would read
+1.06% on the same tape …

Top stock lead: MRK long @ 144.69 — final grade 63
Top option lead: GLD 2026-08-28 $405C long @ 404.8 — final grade 62
Executive memo: TODAY IS AUGUST MONTHLY OPTIONS EXPIRATION - the third Friday …
Slate: 10 stock leads · 10 option leads — every lead carries its entry, stop and target
in the attached PDF.

Research tool — not financial advice. Bablytics is an AI boardroom's research output:
nothing in this email is a recommendation to buy or sell anything, nothing is
personalised to you, and no trade is ever placed for you. Do your own work; if you need
advice, talk to a licensed adviser.

—
Research tool — not financial advice. Bablytics is an AI boardroom's research output;
nothing here is a recommendation or personalised to you.
You receive this because you subscribed at bablytics.com. Reply STOP or visit
https://bablytics.com/unsubscribe.html to stop.

    That is the dry-run text for the 2026-08-21 morning, trimmed only at the ellipses: the draft's body, then the footer the send appends. The attachment was Bablytics-Morning-Briefing-2026-08-21.pdf.

    What every email carries#

    • Plain text. No HTML, no images, no tracking pixel, no link that reports back. The PDF is attached as application/pdf under its own filename.
    • The disclaimer, twice by construction. The drafted body ends with the standing research-tool statement, and render_text appends the footer to every message — "Research tool — not financial advice … You receive this because you subscribed at bablytics.com. Reply STOP or visit <unsubscribe page> to stop." — unless the body already contains that footer line, in which case it is not doubled. A body you write yourself gets it too; you cannot send without it.
    • Headers that say what it is: List-Unsubscribe: <https://bablytics.com/unsubscribe.html> (so mail clients can offer their own unsubscribe button), X-Bablytics-Kind: morning|evening|weekend|custom, Auto-Submitted: no (it was a person), a proper Message-ID and Date.
    • Blind copies. From and To are the From address in Settings; every recipient is in Bcc; fifty per message. The unsubscribe URL in the footer and the header is mail_unsubscribe_url in Settings, default https://bablytics.com/unsubscribe.html.

    Leaving the list: three paths, one result#

    Reply STOP
    Every email says so. The reply lands in your own mailbox — the From address — and you flip the row's toggle (or edit its status) by hand. There is no inbox reader in the app; honouring a STOP is a click you make.
    The unsubscribe page
    bablytics.com/unsubscribe.html writes a document to the create-only collection unsubscribe_requests — {emailLower, createdAt}, nothing else — and the next Sync marks that row unsubscribed with the request date in its notes. Same page is the one the footer and the List-Unsubscribe header point at.
    The toggle in the app
    One click on the row flips active ⇄ unsubscribed and stamps unsubscribed_at. Use it for STOP replies and for anyone who asks you in person.

    All three end the same way: the row stays in the table with status = unsubscribed, it is excluded from every recipient count from then on, and neither a later Sync nor a CSV import without a status column can put it back — only you can, on purpose, with the toggle or an edit. The Firestore rules are create-only, so a person who re-subscribes on the website does not reactivate themselves either; the sync will refresh their name and flags and leave the status alone, and a re-subscribe is your manual call.

    Nothing is automatic. maillist.send() is reached from exactly one place — POST /api/maillist/send, on your click — it renders only unless dry_run is false, and a real send additionally requires confirm: true. The scheduler never imports the module (grep -n maillist bablytics/scheduler.py is empty, and stays empty by the same rule the Broker lives under); the API even carries the policy as a string, policy: "maillist: NOTHING IS SENT AUTOMATICALLY …", so a future UI cannot plead ignorance. The reports are generated on a schedule; sending them is a person's decision, every time.

    The log#

    Every real send — successful, partial or failed, list or test — writes one row to mail_log: sent_at, kind, subject, recipients_count (the addresses actually accepted), the attachment paths, status (ok · partial · failed), the error detail when there is one (which batch, which addresses were refused, or the connection error), and by_user, the signed-in account that clicked. Dry runs are not logged — they send nothing. The tab shows the latest fifty (GET /api/maillist/log?limit=); the table is in bablytics.db like everything else, so a backup of the data folder keeps it.

    API#

    Everything on this page is /api/maillist/…, and every route requires the same signed-in session as the rest of the app.

    GET /api/maillist
    The subscribers (?status=, ?q=), the counts per status and per report kind, which settings are present (never the values), the kind and style lists for the selectors, and the no-autosend policy string.
    POST /api/maillist · PATCH / DELETE /api/maillist/{id} · POST /api/maillist/{id}/toggle
    Add (409 when the address is already on the list), edit, remove, flip active ⇄ unsubscribed.
    POST /api/maillist/import · GET /api/maillist/export.csv
    CSV in ({"csv": "…"} or a raw text/csv body) and out (?status= filter).
    POST /api/maillist/sync
    The Firestore pull → {added, updated, unsubscribed, errors, fetched, synced_at}; 409 with the list of missing settings when not configured.
    GET /api/maillist/draft?kind=&date=
    {kind, date, label, subject, body_text, attachments, missing, sources, headline, recipients_count, ok}. Never fails for a missing day — it says what is missing.
    POST /api/maillist/send
    {kind, subject, body_text, attachments, dry_run (default true), confirm, test_to?}. Dry run → the rendered text, the resolved attachments, recipient and batch counts, would_send. Real send needs dry_run: false and confirm: true; 409 when SMTP is unconfigured; returns sent, status, errors, log_id.
    GET /api/maillist/log
    The send log, newest first.
    GET / PUT /api/maillist/settings
    The effective connection settings with *_password_set flags (never a password); PUT accepts the nine keys listed on the Settings page and refuses any key that looks like a password or a secret.

    Module: bablytics/maillist.py; routes: bablytics/routes_maillist.py; tables: subscribers and mail_log in bablytics/db.py. The website half — the form, the Firestore rules and the one-page project setup — is in site/pages/50-subscribe.html, 51-unsubscribe.html and site/firebase/.
